rules.title: Security deposit cap of one month's rent
rules.requirement: Your landlord cannot demand or take a security deposit of more than one month's rent, on top of first month's rent. A small landlord (a natural person or an LLC of natural persons owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total) may charge up to two months' rent, but not to a service member.
rules.key_value: 1 month rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords)

coverage.summary: All residential rental property used as the tenant's dwelling. Small individual landlords owning no more than two rental properties with four or fewer units in total may charge up to two months' rent, except to service members.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: Security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024
Advance payment of at least six months' rent on a lease of six months or longer

rules.exemptions: Advance payment of not less than six months' rent for leases of six months or longer; mutually agreed paid alterations requested by tenant; small landlords (natural persons or LLCs of natural persons owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four units) may charge up to two months' rent except to service members; does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.
rules.penalty: Bad faith claim or retention of security may subject the landlord to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, plus actual damages.
rules.quoted_span: (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.

rules.title: Higher deposit for service members must be explained and returned after six months
rules.requirement: If you are a service member and are charged a higher-than-standard deposit due to credit or housing history, the landlord must give you a written explanation by lease signing and return the extra amount after no more than six months if you are not behind on rent.

coverage.summary: Residential rentals where the tenant is a service member charged a higher than standard security.

rules.quoted_span: (4) On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security pursuant to paragraph (1) due to the credit history, credit score, housing history, or other factor related to the tenant, the landlord shall provide the tenant with a written statement, on or before the date the lease is signed, of the amount of the higher security and an explanation why the higher security amount is being charged.

rules.title: Deposit return and itemized statement within 21 days; bad-faith penalty
rules.requirement: Within 21 days after you move out, your landlord must return your deposit and give an itemized statement of deductions, with receipts and photos for repair or cleaning charges. Deductions cannot cover ordinary wear and tear, and bad-faith retention can cost the landlord up to twice the deposit plus actual damages.
rules.key_value: 21 calendar days; up to 2x deposit for bad faith

coverage.summary: All residential rental property used as the tenant's dwelling.

rules.exemptions: Documentation requirements do not apply if repair and cleaning deductions total $125 or less or the tenant validly waived them, unless the tenant requests documentation within 14 days.
rules.penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages, for bad faith claim or retention; landlord forfeits claim to security if it fails in bad faith to comply.
rules.quoted_span: (m) The bad faith claim or retention by a landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest of the security or any portion thereof in violation of this section, or the bad faith demand of replacement of security in violation of subdivision (k), may subject the landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.

rules.title: No nonrefundable deposits
rules.requirement: A lease cannot call any deposit or upfront security charge "nonrefundable"; such a clause is not allowed.

coverage.summary: All residential rental property used as the tenant's dwelling.

rules.quoted_span: (n) A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”

notes: Section as amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340 (AB 414), effective January 1, 2026. The one-month cap effective date of 2024-07-01 is inferred from subdivision (c)(6), which excludes security collected before July 1, 2024. Photo documentation requirements (tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025; move-out photos from April 1, 2025) are folded into the return record.
